scope: German legal side, official sources only
method_note: FAST mode, one round. Firecrawl tried once (service.berlin.de/dienstleistung/327261/ returned 404). gesetze-im-internet.de blocked for WebFetch in this session, so statute texts were read via Apify web-fetch (HTTP 200, text matches the statute structure; nothing invented). German statute quotes are recorded in German with an English rendering.

facts.claim: Two non-resident foreigners can register to marry in Germany. § 12 Abs. 1 PStG: the couple register the intended marriage orally or in writing at a Standesamt where one of them has a Wohnsitz or gewöhnlichen Aufenthalt. 'Hat keiner der Eheschließenden Wohnsitz oder gewöhnlichen Aufenthalt im Inland, so ist das Standesamt, vor dem die Ehe geschlossen werden soll, für die Entgegennahme der Anmeldung zuständig.' (If neither has a residence or habitual abode in Germany, the Standesamt before which the marriage is to take place is responsible for receiving the registration.)
facts.publisher: Bundesministerium der Justiz / Bundesamt für Justiz (gesetze-im-internet.de)
facts.authority: Federal law (Personenstandsgesetz); applied by the local Standesamt
facts.use_note: Answer to the lead question: for an Australian couple with no German address, the Anmeldung zur Eheschließung is made at the Standesamt of the town where they want to marry. Do not confuse with Standesamt I in Berlin, which is responsible for issuing Ehefähigkeitszeugnisse to Germans who never lived in Germany (see F-017), not for foreign couples' Anmeldung.

facts.claim: § 12 Abs. 2 PStG: at registration the couple must prove by public documents (öffentliche Urkunden): 1. their civil status (Personenstand), 2. their residence or habitual abode, 3. their nationality, 4. if previously married or in a registered partnership, the last marriage or partnership and its dissolution. If the last marriage was not concluded at a German Standesamt, the dissolution of any further earlier marriages or partnerships must also be proven.
facts.publisher: Bundesministerium der Justiz / Bundesamt für Justiz (gesetze-im-internet.de)
facts.authority: Federal law (PStG); the local Standesamt sets the exact document list
facts.use_note: This is the statutory minimum. The exact list (birth certificate form, passport, translation, apostille) is set by each Standesamt; tell readers to get the list from the Standesamt of their wedding town. § 13 Abs. 1 PStG lets the Standesamt ask for further documents if these are not enough.

facts.claim: § 1309 Abs. 1 BGB: a person whose capacity to marry is governed by foreign law should not marry before producing a certificate from the internal authority of their home state that no impediment to the marriage exists under that state's law (Ehefähigkeitszeugnis). The certificate loses force if the marriage is not concluded within six months of issue, or a shorter period stated on it.
facts.publisher: Bundesministerium der Justiz / Bundesamt für Justiz (gesetze-im-internet.de)
facts.use_note: Whether Australia issues an Ehefähigkeitszeugnis in the § 1309 sense is NOT confirmed by an official source in this batch; see gaps. Do not state 'Australia issues no Ehefähigkeitszeugnis' until DFAT or the German Embassy Canberra confirms it.

facts.claim: § 1309 Abs. 2 BGB: the President of the Oberlandesgericht in whose district the Standesamt where the marriage was registered has its seat can grant an exemption (Befreiung) from producing the Ehefähigkeitszeugnis. The exemption should only be granted to stateless persons habitually resident abroad and to nationals of states whose authorities do not issue Ehefähigkeitszeugnisse in the sense of Abs. 1; in special cases also to nationals of other states. 'Die Befreiung gilt nur für die Dauer von sechs Monaten.' (The exemption is valid for six months only.)
facts.publisher: Bundesministerium der Justiz / Bundesamt für Justiz (gesetze-im-internet.de)
facts.authority: President of the Oberlandesgericht for the district of the registering Standesamt (e.g. Kammergericht for Berlin, OLG München for Munich)
facts.use_note: § 12 Abs. 3 PStG: the Standesamt takes the Befreiung application and prepares the decision, and the couple must supply the evidence needed to check the marriage under the applicable foreign law. Processing time is not stated in law; see gaps.

facts.claim: § 13 Abs. 4 PStG: if no impediment is found, the Standesamt tells the couple the marriage may take place; this notice binds the Standesamt that performs the marriage. 'Sind seit der Mitteilung an die Eheschließenden mehr als sechs Monate vergangen, ohne dass die Ehe geschlossen wurde, so bedarf die Eheschließung erneut der Anmeldung und der Prüfung der Voraussetzungen.' (If more than six months pass after the notice without the marriage, registration and checks must be repeated.)
facts.publisher: Bundesministerium der Justiz / Bundesamt für Justiz (gesetze-im-internet.de)
facts.use_note: So registration is valid six months from the Standesamt's notice. How far ahead a couple may register (earliest date) is not in the statute; check the city page (see gaps).

facts.claim: § 1310 Abs. 1 BGB: 'Die Ehe wird nur dadurch geschlossen, dass die Eheschließenden vor dem Standesbeamten erklären, die Ehe miteinander eingehen zu wollen.' (A marriage is concluded only by the couple declaring before the registrar that they wish to marry each other.) § 1311 BGB: both must make the declaration in person and while present together; it cannot be subject to a condition or time limit.
facts.publisher: Bundesministerium der Justiz / Bundesamt für Justiz (gesetze-im-internet.de)
facts.use_note: Second URL for § 1311: https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bgb/__1311.html. Consequence for the article: in Germany only the civil ceremony before the Standesbeamter creates a legal marriage; a church or celebrant-only ceremony on its own does not. Write it as 'the civil ceremony is the legal one; a religious or symbolic ceremony can follow'. No proxy marriage.

facts.claim: § 1312 BGB: the registrar asks each partner individually whether they wish to marry each other and, after both say yes, pronounces them lawfully married. 'Die Eheschließung kann in Gegenwart von einem oder zwei Zeugen erfolgen, sofern die Eheschließenden dies wünschen.' (The marriage can take place in the presence of one or two witnesses if the couple wish.)
facts.publisher: Bundesministerium der Justiz / Bundesamt für Justiz (gesetze-im-internet.de)
facts.use_note: Witnesses are optional in Germany: zero, one or two, at the couple's wish.

facts.claim: § 1303 BGB (Ehemündigkeit): 'Eine Ehe darf nicht vor Eintritt der Volljährigkeit eingegangen werden. Mit einer Person, die das 16. Lebensjahr nicht vollendet hat, kann eine Ehe nicht wirksam eingegangen werden.' (A marriage may not be entered before reaching majority [18]. A marriage with a person under 16 cannot validly be concluded.)
facts.publisher: Bundesministerium der Justiz / Bundesamt für Justiz (gesetze-im-internet.de)
facts.use_note: Minimum age 18, no exceptions in the current text. Volljährigkeit is 18 under § 2 BGB (not separately fetched).

facts.claim: § 1353 Abs. 1 BGB: 'Die Ehe wird von zwei Personen verschiedenen oder gleichen Geschlechts auf Lebenszeit geschlossen.' (Marriage is concluded for life by two persons of different or the same sex.)
facts.publisher: Bundesministerium der Justiz / Bundesamt für Justiz (gesetze-im-internet.de)
facts.use_note: Same-sex marriage is legal in Germany. Australian recognition of an overseas same-sex marriage is outside this batch's German-law scope.

facts.claim: Berlin (Standesamt, 'Eheschließung anmelden - mit Auslandsbeteiligung'): responsibility rests with the district Standesamt where a partner has a main or secondary residence. 'Hat keiner von Ihnen einen Wohnsitz im Inland, ist das Standesamt zuständig, bei dem die Eheschließung stattfinden soll.' The application can be made at the earliest 6 months before the desired date. Both partners register in person; if both are prevented for important reasons, registration can be made in writing or through an authorised representative; if one is prevented, the other may register alone with written Vollmacht. The registration is valid for 6 months, within which the couple may marry at any German Standesamt.
facts.use_note: Confirms F-001 at city level. Berlin also says a personal consultation at the Standesamt is required before the application, because required documents depend on personal circumstances. The 'earliest 6 months ahead' rule is Berlin's; Munich (F-013) books appointments up to 3 months ahead. Rules are local: say 'in Berlin'.

facts.claim: Berlin: documents not in German must be translated by an interpreter/translator sworn in Germany ('in Deutschland beeidigte/n Dolmetscher/in'). For some countries an Überbeglaubigung (Apostille or Legalisation) is also required; the Apostille (issued by the home country authority) or Legalisation (issued by the German embassy) must be attached directly to the original. All documents must in principle be presented in the original and must not be altered, perforated or laminated.
facts.use_note: Berlin.de/standesamt/ehe repeats: documents in the original and in German, non-German documents translated by an approved, sworn interpreter (directory: justiz-dolmetscher.de). Munich (F-013) accepts translation by a translator recognised in Germany or at a German mission abroad. Whether Australian documents need an apostille for a given Standesamt is not stated; see gaps.

facts.claim: Berlin fees (EUR, page checked 17 Nov 2026): 45.00 registration of the marriage and check of requirements; plus 45.00 per partner for whom foreign law must be considered; an income-based fee if the Befreiung must be applied for at the Kammergericht via the Standesamt; 30.00 statutory declaration (Versicherung an Eides statt); 40.00 marriage at another Standesamt; 80.00 marriage outside opening hours; 75.00 to 150.00 marriage outside the official premises or at branch locations; 12.00 marriage certificate (German); 12.00 multilingual/international marriage certificate; 6.00 each further certificate of the same kind issued at the same time. 'Weitere Kosten können durch besondere Eheschließungsorte entstehen.'
facts.source_date: no page date shown; fees under PStGAV Bln § 9
facts.use_note: Prices are Berlin government fees in EUR, not our prices; write 'Berlin's registry fees in 2026' and do not convert to AUD without Nic. Worked example (two Australians, Berlin, no Befreiung fee yet): 45 + 45 + 45 = 135 EUR before certificates. Present only if Nic approves. Durchführung page (https://service.berlin.de/dienstleistung/318968/) lists the same ceremony fees.

facts.claim: Munich (Landeshauptstadt München, 'Anmeldung einer Eheschließung mit Auslandsbezug'): 'Auslandsbezug' covers a foreign nationality, birth abroad, or a previous marriage or divorce abroad. Couples first need a personal Auskunft (information) on the documents required, for a fee that is credited if they later register. 'Bitte buchen Sie einen Termin, dieser kann bis zu 3 Monate im voraus gebucht werden.' Both attend together with all documents. 'Sie können nicht gut Deutsch, dann bringen Sie eine*n öffentliche bestellte und vereidigte Übersetzer*in mit.' Both partners must be of age and have legal capacity.
facts.use_note: Munich does not state a fee amount on this page. The 3-month figure is the appointment booking window, not the registration validity. Rules differ by city; present Berlin and Munich as examples.

facts.claim: Berlin ceremony rules: witnesses (max. two) may but need not be present ('können, müssen aber nicht anwesend sein'); witnesses must be adults with a valid ID card or passport. 'Falls eine oder beide Personen keine ausreichenden Deutschkenntnisse haben, ist ein vereidigter Dolmetscher erforderlich', arranged by the couple. On the wedding day both partners, and any witnesses and interpreter, must show a valid passport or ID card. After confirmation of the requirements, the marriage can take place within 6 months at any Standesamt in Germany.
facts.use_note: Interpreter wording also on https://service.berlin.de/dienstleistung/318968/ ('ist ein beeidigter Dolmetscher auf Veranlassung der Eheschließenden hinzuzuziehen'). Berlin.de also lists Saturday weddings at some Berlin Standesämter and a page of Berlin wedding rooms; a fee exists for 'Eheschließung außerhalb der Amtsräume' (F-012), but no Berlin page read here names castles or specific outside venues; see gaps.

facts.claim: Kammergericht Berlin (Ehefähigkeitsverfahren): the Befreiung exists because not all states issue Ehefähigkeitszeugnisse; the OLG Presidents, in Berlin the President of the Kammergericht, check instead of the foreign authority whether there is an impediment under the home law. The application is made to the registrar receiving the marriage registration; required documents vary by country. Fee: 'je nach den Einkommensverhältnissen des Antragstellers und des Aufwandes der Sachbearbeitung zwischen 15 EUR und 305 EUR', requested in writing; processing continues only after payment is confirmed. 'Insgesamt müssen Sie mit einer Bearbeitungsdauer von mindestens drei Wochen rechnen', which can be longer if immigration files or further documents are needed. After approval, the papers go back to the Standesamt, which then arranges the wedding date.
facts.use_note: Timing and fee are Berlin's. Other OLGs set their own; a search snippet attributed 4 to 6 weeks to the Hanseatisches OLG (Hamburg) but that page was not read, so do not use it. Write 'at least three weeks in Berlin'. Combined with F-004 (Befreiung valid six months) and F-005 (registration valid six months).

facts.claim: Kammergericht Berlin lists states that currently regularly issue Ehefähigkeitszeugnisse 'u. a.' (among others): Bulgaria, Denmark, Finland, France, Greece, Great Britain, Ireland, Italy, Japan, Kenya, Croatia, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, Mozambique, New Zealand, Netherlands, Norway, Austria, Poland, Portugal, Sweden, Switzerland, Spain, Tanzania, Czech Republic, Turkey, Hungary. Australia is not on the list.
facts.use_note: The list is non-exhaustive ('u. a.'), so Australia's absence does not prove Australia issues no Ehefähigkeitszeugnis. Do NOT write 'Australians need a Befreiung' as settled law. Safe wording: 'Australia is not on the Kammergericht's list of countries that regularly issue a certificate of no impediment in the German sense, so Australians should expect the Standesamt to ask about a Befreiung'. Needs confirmation from the German Embassy Canberra / Consulate General Sydney or DFAT (see gaps).

facts.claim: Auswärtiges Amt: Standesamt I in Berlin is responsible for issuing an Ehefähigkeitszeugnis to a German national who never had (or only temporarily had) a residence or habitual abode in Germany.
facts.use_note: Context only. This concerns Germans marrying abroad. It does NOT mean foreign couples register at Standesamt I; they register at the Standesamt of the wedding town (F-001, F-010). Include only to prevent that mistake.

gaps: Whether Australia issues an Ehefähigkeitszeugnis in the sense of § 1309 BGB, and therefore whether Australians always need the Befreiung: not confirmed by DFAT, the German Embassy Canberra or Consulate General Sydney. australien.diplo.de/au-de/service/05-buergerservice/heirat returned 404 on 17 Nov 2026. Only indirect evidence (F-016).
Whether a German Standesamt requires an apostille on Australian documents: Berlin says 'for some countries' (F-011) without naming Australia. Not confirmed for Australia by an official German source.

Outside venues such as castles (Schloss) as official Trauorte: no city page read here names one. Berlin lists a fee for weddings outside official premises (F-012) and a Trauorte page (https://www.berlin.de/standesamt/ehe/artikel.1593610.php, not read).

Religious ceremonies: no official page read here states the rule on religious ceremonies. Only § 1310 Abs. 1 BGB (F-006) establishes that the marriage is concluded before the Standesbeamter. Do not state anything about church-wedding-before-civil timing.
Hamburg and other cities' fees and Befreiung processing times (OLG Hamburg 4 to 6 weeks appears only in a search snippet, not verified).
Munich fee amounts for the Auskunft, Anmeldung and Trauung: not on the page read.
Recognition in Australia of a German marriage (Marriage Act 1961 Part VA) is outside this batch's German-law scope.
